components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the ocean, the air, and the land

components.text: 1. Evaporation: the Sun Lifts Water Up

The Sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. As the water warms, molecules gain enough energy to escape as water vapour. Plants also release water vapour through their leaves, a process called transpiration.
2. Condensation and Precipitation: Water Falls Back
As water vapour rises, it cools and changes back into tiny liquid droplets, forming clouds. When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
3. Collection: Water Returns to the Ground

Precipitation collects in oceans, lakes, and rivers, or soaks into the ground as infiltration. Groundwater can flow slowly underground and eventually seep back into surface water, completing the cycle.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing one raindrop
components.body: A drop evaporates from a lake on a sunny morning. It rises, cools high in the atmosphere, and joins a cloud. Later it falls as rain on a hillside, soaks into the soil, and eventually reaches a stream that flows back to the lake.
components.code: Lake -> evaporation -> cloud -> condensation -> rain -> infiltration -> stream -> lake
components.code_caption: One full loop of the water cycle
components.takeaway: Water is constantly moving, but the total amount on Earth stays about the same.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when the Sun's energy turns liquid water into vapour.

questions.question: What is the name for water vapour cooling and forming droplets in clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when vapour cools and changes back into liquid droplets.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is any water that falls from clouds, such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
